newsitem.title: UK: Beatles attract new fans as record sales soar.
newsitem.headline: Beatles attract new fans as record sales soar.

text.p: Teenagers born a decade after Beatles disbanded have been buying their records in large numbers, a spokesman for the British pop group said on Monday.
"Figures show that teenagers are by far the biggest group of buyers. You would have thought it would have been middle-aged people," Beatles spokesman Geoff Baker said.
About 41 percent of the people who bought 13 million copies of the Beatles' Anthology 1 and 2 albums this year were teenagers.
Members of the group, which broke up in 1970, are about to celebrate the biggest record receipts in its history with six million sales from their back catalogue.
Gross record sales, TV rights and video sales will earn about 490 million pounds ($780 million) this year with the lion's share going to British record company EMI.
The Beatles' cut will be split among Paul McCartney, George Harrison, Ringo Starr and John Lennon's widow Yoko Ono.
The three surviving Beatles released two albums this year, with two songs featuring recordings Lennon made before he was shot dead in 1980.
The third Beatles album, Anthology 3, which covers the Beatles' recordings from 1966-70, will be released on October 28. The group has said Anthology 3 will be its final album.
